definition: putting something between my own surfaces, because the touch registers twice

settled:
Skin on skin lands on both sides at once, so the signal is delivered twice on a system already paying too much per input. The inside of an arm resting on my torso is felt by the arm and by the torso together.

I find my own skin touching my own skin irritating for that reason. It is not aesthetic and not psychological. It is a tactile signal counted twice.

Any layer breaks it. Sleeves, a shirt, trousers, socks, a pillow between the knees or between arm and torso when I lie on my side.

Loose works as well as tight, because the layer does not have to grip. Tight clothing does two other jobs, grounding me and damping touch, and this is a separate mechanism sharing the tool. So swapping to loose loses the grounding and not this.

Posture counts too: not clasping hands, not sitting with the knees together, and shifting a limb off another when contact lands.

This and the lotion are one class. Each holds a layer in place all the time and puts it back when something disturbs it.

title: Keeping My Skin Off My Skin
